text:
incident-bot: HIGH: Tenant-facing NLB healthcheck failures for customer 'OrchidFinance' (private VPC vc-09f). Observed 5xx at edge, start 2026-03-14T13:02:10Z. Paging @sre-oncall @network-oncall :rotating_light:

maria_ng: ack — I'm here, adding context: affected pool is DedicatedPool-7 (dp-7), ingress via cross-account NLB in us-west-2, Route53 private hosted zone. Customer reports intermittent 504s when traffic spikes.

ashok_k: looking at NLB metrics now — TargetGroup tg-0a3 shows targetHealth Unhealthy 3/6, reason=TLS handshake timeout and failed health checks.

leo_t: seeing backend logs show connection resets after 2m idle, not immediate. Could be ephemeral port NAT or SG egress blocking return traffic.

sre-oncall: running quick probe from our probe runner to the tenant endpoint -> curl times out intermittently. Attaching snippet:
```
$ curl -v --connect-timeout 5 https://tenant.orchid.internal/health
* Connected to nlb-12345 (10.10.5.2) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.2 connection established
* Empty reply from server
```

network-oncall: checking VPC flow logs for 13:00-13:10Z window, will filter by src/dst ports and SG ids.

sarah_cs: customer confirmation: we pushed a tighter egress security group at 12:58Z that restricts ephemeral port range to specific CIDRs as a compliance change. They didn't expect it to affect internal LB health checks.

maria_ng: ok that aligns — health checks from the NLB originate from within our peered VPC CIDR 10.20.0.0/16, which may be outside their allowed list. Plan suggestion: 1) request customer to temporarily relax egress SG to allow 10.20.0.0/16 ephemeral ports, 2) spin up an ALB inside customer VPC as an ingress fallback (private) and shift DNS weights 3) monitor.

ashok_k: customer approval required for SG change. Sarah: can you confirm they give us go for temporary rule?

sarah_cs: customer approves temporary SG change for mitigation window up to 1 hour. They asked us to do minimal scope.

maria_ng: executing canary: will add a single ingress rule for ephemeral TCP high-ports from 10.20.0.0/16 -> sg-0f4 temporarily. Command I will run (IAM: infra-admin):
```bash
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0f4abcd --protocol tcp --port 32768-61000 --cidr 10.20.0.0/16 --description "temp: allow NLB healthchecks for OrchidFinance mitigation"
```

deploy-bot: change request created: CR-4872 by maria_ng — pending manual approval.

sre_admin: noted — mig window and auditor tag required. I'll sign off after chat confirmation. :white_check_mark:

ashok_k: after applying SG change, rechecking target health...

leo_t: targetHealth now 6/6, healthchecks passing for 2m. Metrics: healthy_count back to normal, latency stabilized ~18ms.

maria_ng: starting weighted DNS shift to route 20% traffic to standby tenant pool (dp-7-backup) to validate stability under load. Using Route53 weighted records. Command: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets` with weight 20/80.

network-oncall: flow logs confirm SYN/ACK flows returning for NLB healthcheck source IPs after SG change. No drops seen.

sarah_cs: customer monitoring shows user-facing errors dropping to near zero on their side.

maria_ng: good. keep canary 15min, if stable increase to 50% then full. rolling docs: if errors exceed 1% in 5min window, rollback to original routing and revert SG.

leo_t: note: root cause is customer compliance SG change that inadvertently blocked our internal healthcheck CIDR. Recommend we add a preventative note to onboarding docs: required ephemeral port allowances and our healthcheck source CIDRs.

ashok_k: follow-up actions: 1) create runbook entry for NLB healthcheck SG interaction, 2) reach out to infra product to add explicit SG template in Private deploy guide, 3) schedule post-incident RCA with customer and account team.

maria_ng: raising PD incident to P1->P2 transition, adding RCA owners. Incident ticket: PD-2719, containment achieved at 13:07Z.

incident-bot: PD-2719 status updated: Contained — mitigation applied (SG temporary rule + DNS shift).

sre-oncall: moving to monitoring, handing off to rotation for 2h watch — @network-oncall please follow for next checks.

network-oncall: ack. I'll monitor healthchecks, NLB metrics, and route53 propagation. If any reoccurrence, escalate to on-call infra.

maria_ng: thanks everyone — documenting notes, will attach timeline and commands to the incident ticket. Postmortem will cover communication and pre-prod validation for SG changes. :memo:
